title: City payees confirmed as State-licensed care operators, and what regulators record about their sites
question: Which companies the City pays for care are, on two keys, the operators of State-licensed facilities, and what do State and federal regulators record about those facilities?
finding: 23 City payees paid $100,000 or more are confirmed as the operator of a State-licensed health facility by two keys: the payee's own City business registration sits at the licensed address, and that registration carries the facility's or the licensee's name. The City paid them $1,466.0 million. 6 of them hold sites with State enforcement actions since 2021 (21 actions, 2 citations of class AA or A, $324,000 in final penalties). Largest private operators with a regulator's record or a large related-company balance: CRESTWOOD BEHAVIORAL HEALTH INC ($191.1 million from DPH; 1 confirmed and 22 other sites under the same licensee; 12 State action(s), 0 of class AA or A; net income $13.6 million on revenue of $118.9 million at its 5 site(s) filing a State nursing-home report for 2025); Sequoia Living ($12.8 million from HSA, HOM, MYR; 1 confirmed and 2 other sites under the same licensee; 1 State action(s), 0 of class AA or A; net income $-2.2 million on revenue of $13.6 million at its 3 site(s) filing a State nursing-home report for 2025; $1.2 million owed by related companies); Planned Parenthood Northern California ($637,000 from DPH; 1 confirmed and 16 other sites under the same licensee; 2 State action(s), 0 of class AA or A); Garfield Nursing Home Inc ($581,859 from DPH; 2 confirmed and 0 other sites under the same licensee; 3 State action(s), 2 of class AA or A; net income $2.5 million on revenue of $27.7 million at its 2 site(s) filing a State nursing-home report for 2025; $55.4 million owed by related companies); River Vista Behavioral Health ($369,113 from DPH; 1 confirmed and 0 other sites under the same licensee; 2 State action(s), 0 of class AA or A); MEDICAL HILL HEALTHCARE CENTER ($336,220 from DPH; 1 confirmed and 0 other sites under the same licensee; 1 State action(s), 0 of class AA or A; net income $5.1 million on revenue of $30.2 million at its 1 site(s) filing a State nursing-home report for 2025; $45.2 million owed by related companies). The middle California nursing home with $2 million or more of revenue reported net income of 7.3% of revenue in 2025. 1 payee(s) began their latest City contract within 24 months after a class AA or A citation or an immediate-jeopardy penalty at a confirmed site: Garfield Nursing Home Inc (DPH - Skilled Nursing Facility (no. 1000038024), from 2026-07-01 to 2029-03-31, $6.6 million agreed; 2025-10-23: class A citation at Garfield Neurobehavioral Center, $25,000, under appeal; 2025-11-24: class AA citation at Garfield Neurobehavioral Center, $75,000, under appeal).
how: City payees with $100,000 or more in the Controller's payment file were looked up in the Treasurer's business registry by owner name and trade name. A payee is confirmed when one of its registered locations has the same street address and ZIP code as a facility in the State Public Health listing of open licensed facilities or the State Health Care Services list of mental health rehabilitation centers, and the registration at that address carries the facility's name or the licensee's name. Other sites are facilities elsewhere whose licensee has exactly the same legal name as a confirmed one. Revenue, net income and the related-company balance are added up over those sites that file a State nursing-home financial report (latest year), so they describe the operator's reporting homes, not the City contract. For those sites: State enforcement actions from the dashboard (January 2021 to 13 November 2026) by State facility number; federal fines from the October 2026 federal nursing-home file by certification number; the latest State financial report by report number. The latest City contract is the one with the latest start date in the Controller's contract file whose prime contractor carries the payee's name.
limits: A City payment may be for a different site or service than the one cited, and large hospital systems appear here simply because they are licensed and paid. State actions include small administrative penalties. Class AA and A citations carry the largest citation penalties in the dashboard file (middle first-assessed penalty $120,000 and $25,000, against $3,000 for class B); an action shown as open and under appeal has not been upheld, and penalties are often reduced or dismissed. A contract that begins after a citation may replace an earlier arrangement for the same beds, and the City may use a different home of the operator than the one cited. Mental health rehabilitation centers are licensed by a different State department whose enforcement record is not on file, so a zero there means no record on disk, not a clean record. An amount owed by related companies is a claim the home holds, common where a chain pools cash.
